parameter: HULL_HALF (hull box half extents; R_IN, R_OUT)
source: (a) manufacturer: BlueROV2 Heavy 457 x 575 x 254 mm (the Heavy kit moves two extra thrusters outside the frame); independent CAD (von Benzon Table 5): 0.46 x 0.38 x 0.58 m, height larger than the manufacturer's 254 mm (R1 1.1)
derivation: half extent = dimension / 2 (0.2285 / 0.2875 / 0.127 m, rounded up by 0.5 mm); R_IN = min half extent = 0.127 m; R_OUT = norm of the half extents = 0.389 m
validity: Bare vehicle as sold. A payload that enlarges the envelope (CAD height 0.38 m) needs a larger R_OUT, which enters Envelope.d_upper_offset; a box only bounds an open frame

parameter: Vehicle mass (HoloOcean MassInKG; not set by the repository)
source: (a) Heavy kit page: 11.5 kg (26 lb) with ballast; BlueROV2 page 11-12 kg; Wu 2018 Table 5.1: 11.5 kg; von Benzon Table A1: 13.5 kg measured (R1 1.2)
derivation: surge inertia with added mass would be 13.5 + 6.36 = 19.9 kg (von Benzon), 55 % above the simulated 11.5 kg
validity: The engine models no added mass; this mainly affects transients such as braking, which are calibrated in closed loop in the simulator (see a_brake)

parameter: Thruster force limit per unit command
source: project choice, conservative against every source (R1 1.4 verdict: DERIVED, class d): T200 forward thrust 36.4 N at 12 V and 51.5 N at 16 V; von Benzon regression F(1) = 30.4 N; Gabl whole-vehicle bollard force 92 N forward; HoloOcean clamp 28.75 N (R1 1.4)
derivation: 12 N is 33 % of the T200 at 12 V and 23 % at 16 V. Four horizontal thrusters at 45 deg give 4 x 12 / sqrt(2) = 33.9 N of surge force at full command (37-40 % of the 85-92 N of a real vehicle) and 13.6 N at the nominal authority 0.40 (about 15 %)
validity: T200 figures are bench data at fixed voltage. Not modelled: thruster deadzone and about 0.08 s thruster lag. State that the simulated horizontal thrust is about 0.15 (nominal) to 0.4 (full) of a real Heavy

parameter: AUTHORITY: cap of the normalised horizontal command (nominal / brake / escape)
source: no external source; controller design inside the simulator control scheme 0 (thruster forces) (R1 section 0)
derivation: effective force along one axis 0.40 / 0.50 / 0.60 x 33.9 N = 13.6 / 17.0 / 20.4 N
validity: Bounds the control-feasible envelope (control/current_envelope.py); not a vehicle property

parameter: HoloOcean engine hydrodynamics (drag coefficient, area, damping)
source: inherited simulator constants, no cited source. Literature differs widely: von Benzon (pool, tether) quadratic surge damping 141.0 N s^2/m^2; Wu 2018 18.18 (values taken from another vehicle); Gabl 16.4 N measured at 0.6 m/s (R1 2.4)
derivation: surge drag at 0.6 m/s through the water: von Benzon 59.0 N, Wu 9.0 N, Gabl 16.4 N, simulator 11.0 N; the simulator is 0.67 of Gabl and 0.19 of von Benzon
validity: Isotropic quadratic drag cannot represent the measured anisotropy (141 / 217 / 190 N s^2/m^2 in surge / sway / heave). Call the plant HoloOcean default dynamics calibrated in closed loop, not BlueROV2 hydrodynamics

parameter: Steady-command curve g(r) = abs(r) / 2.4 + 0.203 r^2 (surge/sway slope, quadratic term, tolerance)
source: (from simulator calibration, class d) calibration/probe_head_current_authority.py, largest residual 5.3 % (DESIGN_ITERATIONS DI-27)
derivation: multiplying by 33.9 N gives F_sim(r) = 14.1 r + 6.9 r^2 N; at nominal authority the through-water speed is 0.70-0.71 m/s, not the 0.96 m/s predicted by the small-signal slope
validity: Valid up to about 0.71 m/s through the water (highest calibrated speed); closed loop with the DVL velocity loop, 0.1 s period and the 12 N limit; not a hardware figure

parameter: Heave slope
source: (from simulator calibration, calibration/probe_motion.py) small-signal slope; 48 N per unit heave command
derivation: feasibility check: vertical bollard thrust of the Heavy 14 kgf (137 N); von Benzon heave limit 0.71 m/s at 120 N
validity: Feasible for the declared 0.25 m/s vertical current (about 20 N from the von Benzon drag model, 15 % of 137 N)

parameter: Commanded current to steady drift of an unactuated vehicle (horizontal and vertical tables)
source: (from simulator calibration, calibration/probe_current.py) HoloOcean applies the current through quadratic drag on the relative velocity; Unreal linear damping acts on the body velocity
derivation: a commanded 1.0 m/s produces only 0.117 m/s of drift; Envelope current values are effective drifts
validity: Simulator convention only; same table for the vertical component

parameter: Closing deceleration per drone
source: (from simulator calibration, class d) stop from 0.446-0.455 m/s in 0.6 s over 0.098-0.104 m: 0.743-0.758 m/s^2 from the stop time and 0.994-1.021 m/s^2 from the stop distance (R1 2.3)
derivation: open-loop bound from von Benzon: (13.5 + 6.36 kg) with 85 N reverse force gives 4.3 m/s^2 at zero speed; Gabl 86 N backward with 11.5 + 6.36 kg gives 4.8 m/s^2. a_brake is about 1/9 of the open-loop bound and 0.67 of the simulator figure
validity: Closed-loop simulator figure (DVL velocity loop, no added mass, 12 N limit); physically conservative; to be re-measured on hardware. No BlueROV2 braking measurement was found in the literature

parameter: Survey speed
source: mission design choice; R1 2.1 verdict SUPPORTED as feasible: 42 % of von Benzon's identified surge limit (0.72 m/s) and 20 % of the manufacturer's 1.5 m/s
derivation: feasibility only; the two capability sources differ by a factor of about 2 (0.72 m/s identified, about 1.4-1.5 m/s manufacturer and Gabl)
validity: Not a physical constant. The simulator reaches 0.71 m/s through the water at nominal authority

parameter: Cruise cap outside avoidance and escape speed
source: design caps; R1 2.2 verdict SUPPORTED as feasible in still water under both capability sources
derivation: a lateral escape at 0.55 m/s with the residual drift w_drift_max = 0.15 m/s needs up to 0.70 m/s through the water
validity: 0.70 m/s exceeds von Benzon's identified sway limit (0.63 m/s) but not the capability implied by Gabl's forces: flag lateral escape against a cross current as marginal in a hardware claim

parameter: Horizontal current exercised
source: (a) Blue Robotics FAQ: operate in currents no stronger than 1-1.5 knots (0.51-0.77 m/s); (b) Gabl hold force 16.4 N at 0.6 m/s (18 % of 92 N thrust); no site current statistics were opened (R1 3.1)
derivation: effective drift of an unactuated vehicle (Envelope convention); at the 0.30 m/s survey speed the authority already stops at about 0.41 m/s head current (calibration), 0.60 m/s lateral is held without saturation
validity: Exercised range, not a controllability bound (DI-27). Do not present simulated loads as real hydrodynamic loads

parameter: Vertical current declared
source: no source on vertical current magnitudes was opened (R1 3.2)
derivation: feasibility only: heave capability 14 kgf vertical bollard thrust; von Benzon drag model gives about 20 N at 0.25 m/s
validity: Declared, not binding (separate heave channel), no empirical basis

parameter: DVL geometry and rate (beam elevation, MaxRange, report rate)
source: (a) Water Linked DVL A50 datasheet v5: 1 MHz, 4-beam Janus, beam angle 22.5 deg, ping rate 4-15 Hz (adaptive), maximum altitude 50 m (above 35 m depends on seabed conditions); TCP JSON report rate 2-15 Hz (R1 4.1)
derivation: none (values copied)
validity: Ping rate and bottom lock depend on altitude; a fixed 10 Hz lies inside the published range

parameter: dvl_vel_sigma (per-beam velocity noise)
source: (a) Nortek DVL1000: single-ping std 0.8 cm/s at 1.5 m/s; Wayfinder on a BlueROV2 Heavy: 10 mm/s at 1.5 m/s (vendor reprint); 600 kHz Explorer 0.01 m/s (Spielvogel Table VI); A50 publishes no single-ping noise (R1 4.2). Conservative
derivation: HoloOcean applies VelSigma per beam; body-frame horizontal std = sigma_b / (sqrt(2) sin 22.5 deg) = 1.85 sigma_b, vertical 0.54 sigma_b: LOW 1.85 cm/s, MEDIUM 2.8 cm/s (probe: 0.0184, 0.0188, 0.0054 m/s at 0.01). White noise adds 0.055 m (LOW) and 0.083 m (MEDIUM) to a 90 s dead-reckoning run
validity: Vendor values are at 1.5 m/s; the vehicles fly at 0.55 m/s or less near the seabed, so the comparison is conservative. Nortek and Wayfinder do not state per-beam or per-component

parameter: DVL long-term (scale-factor) error
source: omission (R1 4.3): A50 Standard long-term accuracy +-1.01 %; Nortek license-free above 1 %; Wayfinder scale factor within +-1.15 %. The model has white noise only
derivation: an along-track error of up to 1 % of the distance travelled (0.3 m over a 30 m approach)
validity: Open issue O-4. R1 recommends a per-run, per-drone scale factor uniform in +-1 % for LOW and MEDIUM, or an explicit statement of the omission

parameter: dvl_range_sigma (per-beam range noise)
source: neither the A50 datasheet nor the docs overview gives an altitude or range accuracy (R1 4.4)
derivation: small next to seabed_tol_m = 0.70 m
validity: Label as an assumption

parameter: DVL dropout per sample and outage windows (bottom-lock loss)

value.outage: MEDIUM only: 1.0 s, mean period 60 s

source: causes documented qualitatively (altitude, bubbles from thrusters, blocked beams, lock cycling every 10 s in tanks); no frequency or duration statistic for small vehicles was found (R1 4.5)
derivation: partial-beam windows used in the literature are 5-30 s (Cohen and Klein, their test design), much longer than the 1 s outage
validity: Keep as stress setting; a single-factor screen with 5-30 s outages would be informative

parameter: imu_accel_sigma (accelerometer white noise, 30 Hz)
source: (a) ICM-20602 accelerometer noise 100 ug/sqrt(Hz) (TDK 2019, InvenSense 2015); 3DM-GX5-25 0.0075 m/s^2 at 20 Hz (Spielvogel Table VI). At or above the datasheet (R1 5.2)
derivation: sigma = 9.81e-4 sqrt(B) m/s^2: 3.8e-3 at 15 Hz bandwidth and 9.8e-3 at 100 Hz; ours is 1.0-2.6x (LOW) and 2.0-5.3x (MEDIUM)
validity: Used for roll and pitch only. The output filter bandwidth of the real Navigator/ArduSub pipeline is not verified

parameter: imu_gyro_sigma (gyro white noise, 30 Hz)
source: (a) ICM-20602 gyro noise 0.004 dps/sqrt(Hz); 3DM-GX5-25 0.00025 rad/s. Very conservative (R1 5.3)
derivation: 0.004 dps/sqrt(Hz) = 6.98e-5 rad/s/sqrt(Hz): 2.7e-4 rad/s at 15 Hz, 7.0e-4 at 100 Hz; ours is 7-18x (LOW) and 14-37x (MEDIUM)
validity: Used for yaw-rate damping only. The excess may represent unquantified thruster vibration: label as an upper bound

parameter: IMU bias random-walk steps (accelerometer, gyro; per 30 Hz sample)
source: no in-run stability specification was opened; the ICM-20602 datasheet DS-000176 (ZRO tolerance) could not be retrieved (R1 5.4). Order of magnitude of an uncalibrated MEMS offset (Kinsey: 1-5 deg/s); far above a calibrated AHRS (A50 yaw drift 0.1-0.3 deg per minute)
derivation: bias(T) = sigma_step sqrt(30 T). After 90 s: gyro bias 0.30 deg/s (LOW), 0.89 deg/s (MEDIUM); accel bias 0.010 / 0.026 m/s^2; equivalent tilt error 0.06 / 0.15 deg
validity: Sample-rate dependent (sigma_step x sqrt(f)). Limited effect: gyro and accelerometer do not enter the horizontal position estimate

parameter: heading_bias_deg, LOW (constant compass bias, sign from the seed)
source: (b) best case only: calibrated compasses reach 1-3 deg (Kinsey); MMC5983MA 1.0 deg typical; MAVBE about 1 deg; 0.55 deg after MAGYC in one experiment (R1 6.1)
derivation: a constant bias b gives a cross-track dead-reckoning error D sin b = 0.87 % of the distance travelled
validity: Keep only as best-case in-situ calibration. Open issue O-5 (R1: raise to 1.0 deg or label as best case)

parameter: heading_bias_deg, MEDIUM
source: (b) properly calibrated magnetic heading 1-3 deg (Kinsey 2.2.1); Rypkema SandShark about 3 deg 1-sigma after calibration; Spielvogel TWOSTEP 2.88 / 2.60 deg; uncalibrated 23-28 deg (R1 6.1)
derivation: D sin b = 3.49 % of the distance travelled
validity: Literature values are calibration residuals; real errors also depend on heading (soft iron) and vary with thruster currents. The simulated magnetic vector is horizontal, so tilt-coupled errors are absent. The Rypkema 3 deg is read from the ar5iv rendering, which prints 33 deg (typesetting artefact): confirm in the PDF

parameter: mag_sigma (magnetometer white noise per axis of a unit field, 30 Hz)
source: (a) MMC5983MA total RMS noise 0.4-1.2 mG; 3DM-GX5-25 0.002 gauss; VN100 1 mG. Conservative for the chip (R1 6.2)
derivation: heading std is about 57.3 sigma deg: 0.29 / 0.57 / 1.15 deg per sample (probe: 0.29, 0.56, 1.16)
validity: Real heading error is dominated by calibration residuals, not chip noise. Heading is atan2(m_y, m_x) of the raw sample (nav.py, no filter)

parameter: depth_sigma (pressure depth, 30 Hz)
source: (a) MS5837-30BA resolution 0.20 mbar RMS at OSR 8192 (0.28-1.57 mbar at lower OSR); Bar30 resolution 2 mm; conservative (R1 7)
derivation: 0.02 m is about 1.96 mbar, 10x the best RMS resolution; 0.03 m about 15x
validity: The absolute offset (about +-0.5 m at 0-6 bar) is removed by zeroing at the surface and is not modelled; water-density setting and surface waves are not modelled

parameter: latency_s, transport (all onboard streams)
source: (a) Water Linked TCP JSON message latency about 4 ms average, 2 ms std, 13 ms observed maximum (R1 9.1). Data are delivered late but stamped with the capture time (sim/holo_env.py)
derivation: a velocity delay tau offsets the dead-reckoning position by v tau: 0.015 m at 0.05 s (0.30 m/s)
validity: Supported as transport latency only; see the next two rows for the DVL measurement age and the other streams

parameter: latency_s, DVL measurement age (time of validity to delivery)
source: weak evidence, two sources (R1 9.1): von Benzon Table 1 gives a DVL delay of 0.1 s; the Water Linked docs example gives time_of_transmission minus time_of_validity = 0.189 s (one example, not a statistic)
derivation: v tau at 0.30 m/s: 0.03 m (0.1 s), 0.057 m (0.19 s); adds phase lag to the DVL velocity loop
validity: Open issue O-3: the code applies one latency to every stream (no separate DVL age). R1 recommends 0.1-0.2 s for the DVL in MEDIUM

parameter: latency_s, IMU, compass, depth
source: no latency data found for these streams (R1 9.1); Nortek proprietary format gives 1 ms time-stamp accuracy only
derivation: none
validity: Keep as assumption

parameter: Dead-reckoning drift envelope implied by heading bias (cross-track share of distance)
source: (b) R1 8: 0.2-10 % of the distance travelled in the literature, 2-5 % typical for modestly priced units and 0.1 % for the best INS (Paull); 0.4 % over five-hour missions (Kinsey); 10 % reduced to 0.2-0.5 % with MAGYC; SandShark without a DVL 2-10 %
derivation: D sin b with b = 0.5 / 2.0 deg; DVL white noise adds less than 0.1 m per run; a missing 1 % scale factor would add up to 1 % along track
validity: LOW and MEDIUM lie inside the published range. Consistency issue with AcousticConfig.nav_err_gate_m: open issue O-6

parameter: IMU, compass and depth rates
source: simulator configuration (R1 section 0); IMU/compass/depth publish rates are not tied to a datasheet
derivation: none
validity: Output filter bandwidths and stream latencies of the real Navigator/ArduSub pipeline are not verified

parameter: NoiseProfile HIGH (all fields)
source: pure stress level beyond the declared operating domain (out-of-envelope checks); not a validation level (sensor_noise.py)
derivation: none
validity: No provenance is claimed for HIGH values; they are excluded from VALIDATION_LEVELS

parameter: Sonar suite: six SinglebeamSonar, one per hull face (mount positions)
source: no source describes a six-face suite of wide single beams on a small ROV; the closest published concept is a nine-beam forward-looking sonar for small AUVs (Morency et al.). R2 1a: design assumption with a derived coverage requirement
derivation: six cones on the body axes cover the sphere only if the half-angle is at least arccos(1/sqrt(3)) = 54.74 deg (cube-corner directions); margin at 60 deg is 5.26 deg. Mounts = HULL_HALF + 1 cm
validity: HoloOcean has no acoustic interference between transmitters; 36 co-located sonars pinging at 10 Hz (six drones) would need frequency or code separation on real hardware. Describe the layout as a coverage requirement, not a product

parameter: Cone opening (full angle, hard-edged in HoloOcean)
source: R2 1b design assumption: no conical single-beam proximity sonar of comparable width was found. Widest conical single beams: 20-25 deg (Ping 25 deg at -3 dB, Imagenex 852 20 deg with 330 kHz option), 60 deg at -10 dB for a fish-finder transducer; 120-130 deg exists only as the horizontal fan of multibeam imaging sonars
derivation: directivity index of an ideal uniform cone D = 4 pi / Omega: 6.0 dB at 120 deg versus 19.3 dB at 25 deg, about 13 dB less per pass for the same transducer
validity: HoloOcean applies a hard cone with uniform sensitivity (probe: detection up to 60 deg off-axis, 62.5 deg at 3 m). Call the sensor an idealised wide-beam range-only sensor, never a commercial device

parameter: RangeMin
source: (a) Ping typical minimum range 0.3 m; MicronEchosounder 0.3-50 m; S500 minimum 0.3 m (Imagenex 852: 0.5 m) (R2 1c)
derivation: none
validity: Mapping holds for the minimum range only (blind zone), not for the beamwidth. Hard cut in HoloOcean; hulls at contact distance lie inside the blind zone, safety relies on acting earlier (d_safe 1.0 m)

parameter: RangeMax
source: R2 1d design assumption: hard cut-off; narrow-beam products reach 50-100 m on large targets, no source gives a detection range for a BlueROV2-size target with a 120 deg beam
derivation: none
validity: HoloOcean bin intensity does not decay with range: detection is 100 % up to RangeMax and 0 beyond (probe: 100 % at 11 m, 0 % at 12.5 m)

parameter: Range bins (width)
source: (a) mapped: Ping resolution 0.5 % of scan range gives 6 cm at 12 m; dedicated echosounders resolve 1-20 mm (R2 1e)
validity: Resolution is not accuracy: no opened single-beam datasheet states a range accuracy

parameter: Capture rate
source: (a) S500 maximum 10 pings/s; (b) nine-beam small-AUV prototype pinged about every 0.1 s in field trials; multibeams 5-97 Hz (R2 1f)
derivation: two-way travel time at 12 m is 24 m / 1480 m/s = 16 ms, compatible with 10 Hz
validity: Order of magnitude only. Simultaneous pinging of six co-located transducers is not covered by any source

parameter: Detection threshold (HoloOcean intensity units)
source: (from simulator measurement, class d, and DI-11) with add 0.05, mult 0.1, range 0.05: false alarms per capture 98 % at 0.15, 6.7 % at 0.20, 0 % at 0.25 and above (60 empty captures); a BlueROV2 at 1-8 m detected in 100 % of captures up to 0.70; target peaks 0.9-1.2 (R2 2a)
derivation: T / sigma_add = 6.0 / 5.0 / 4.0; per-bin tail exp(-T^2 / (2 sigma^2)) = 1.5e-8 / 3.7e-6 / 3.4e-4
validity: Intensity is R^2 cos averaged per bin, not a calibrated echo level; noise is stationary, whereas real detectors adapt the threshold to range and environment

parameter: sonar_add_sigma, CLEAN (Rayleigh scale of the additive intensity noise)
source: (from simulator measurement, class d) probe fit of the Rayleigh scale 0.0496 for 0.05; exceedances 0 / 1 / 8 / 44 / 296 observed against 0.0 / 1.2 / 10.3 / 45.2 / 283.8 expected for 0.05 / 0.07 / 0.08 / 0.09 / 0.11 (R2 2b)
derivation: HoloOcean uses AddSigma as the Rayleigh scale (std of each Gaussian component); the std of the added noise is 0.655 AddSigma
validity: No source ties a HoloOcean intensity sigma to a physical noise level

parameter: sonar_add_sigma, LOW and MEDIUM
source: no measured false-alarm rate for small-vehicle sonars was found (R2 2b). The exact Rayleigh formula is optimistic against shallow-water field data, which show heavier tails (Lyons and Abraham; Gallaudet and de Moustier)
derivation: per capture and sonar (234 bins): 8.7e-4 (LOW), 7.6e-2 (MEDIUM, 4.5 false alarms per drone per second); confirmed 2-of-3 ghosts per drone per second 8.2e-6 (LOW), 0.064 (MEDIUM, one every 16 s)
validity: Report as T/sigma (5 and 4). The archived anchor (transponder-ranging outlier rates) is a different device and does not support the value. A K or Rayleigh-mixture wrapper would be the literature-backed heavy-tailed option (not implemented)

parameter: sonar_mult_sigma (normal, multiplicative, per occupied bin)
source: convention of HoloOcean (ICRA 2022 Eq. 2; IROS 2022 Eq. 12); no value is given for a single-beam echosounder. Effect measured in the probe: peak p05-p95 widens from 0.90-1.20 (0.10) to 0.93-1.52 (0.30); MEDIUM 0.25 was not probed (R2 2c)
derivation: fade gain 0.2 assumes peaks of at most 1.5 (0.2 x 1.5 = 0.30 = threshold); at MEDIUM the upper tail can approach that
validity: Minor: a few faded captures may still contain the echo

parameter: sonar_range_sigma (exponential mean of the per-leaf range diffusion)
source: HoloOcean model (IROS 2022 Sec. III-D: exponential range diffusion as an approximation of a K-distribution model); no value is given for any device (R2 2d)
derivation: in code the value is the mean (= std) of a one-sided exponential, one draw per leaf; the leading edge is the minimum over many leaves and barely moves (p95 +0.044 m, max +0.094 m up to 0.40) while the far tail grows like sigma ln N
validity: Not a standard deviation of the echo edge. MEDIUM 0.10 m versus structure_tol_far_m 0.70: open issue O-2
code_action: none; open issue O-2 (see structure tolerances)

parameter: sonar_range_jitter_m, LOW (whole-profile shift, quantised to 5 cm bins)
source: R2 3b: the archived anchor (Ping resolution 0.5 % of range) is a misread, because the Ping page labels the resolution relative to the waterfall (scan) range and a quantisation step is not a standard deviation; the physical motivation in sensor_noise.py (timing or sound-speed fluctuation) does not fit a range-independent shift
derivation: shift k = round(N(0, sigma) / 0.05 m) bins (holo_env._degrade); P(k >= 1) = 4.8 %, P(k >= 2) = 2.9e-7 per side
validity: Consistent with eps_range for hull echoes at LOW (3e-7 per side)

parameter: sonar_range_jitter_m, MEDIUM
source: R2 3b: contradicts the declared Envelope. P(k >= 1) = 20.2 %, P(k >= 2) = 6.2e-3 per side; with the measured hull baselines (+0.044 / +0.054 m far side, -0.006 m near side) k = +2 gives +0.144 to +0.154 m against eps_range_far = 0.12 m and k = -2 gives -0.106 m against -0.08 m
derivation: about 1.2 % of MEDIUM captures (0.62 % per side) violate eps_range for hull echoes
validity: Open issue O-1. Values unchanged (checked): holo_env._degrade shifts by any k, no truncation at +-1 bin; Envelope.eps_range unchanged. The exceedance is now declared in the sensor_noise.py docstring and in the eps_range_far comment (stress level, outside the proved P1 envelope)
code_action: changed: exceedance declared in code comments; values unchanged; open issue O-1

parameter: sonar_dropout (capture lost, per capture and sonar)
source: no source found for small-vehicle sonar capture loss (R2 3c)
derivation: one lost capture gives age 0.1 s + latency; two consecutive losses (1e-4 at 1 %) reach 0.25 s with the MEDIUM latency 0.05 s, the boundary of age <= tau_max (R2 convention, see O-7)
validity: Stress setting

parameter: sonar_fade_prob and sonar_fade_gain (missed detection: the capture arrives, the target echo does not)
source: the archived anchor (Kaeli et al. 2019, 10 % no-return in a simulation) concerns transponder ranging, not echo detection, and its numbers were not re-verified (R2 3d). Real misses depend on range, target strength and SNR, which HoloOcean does not model
derivation: the 2-of-3 confirmation loses a target when two of the last three captures fade: 3.0e-4 (1 %), 2.7e-3 (3 %)
validity: The sector stays healthy and its silence would be trusted: the hazardous case. Code action: EchoHold (commit 31efb0d, perception/targets.py) holds the nearest obstacle echo of every healthy sector for tau_max, so a single missed capture becomes a stale reading; consecutive misses longer than tau_max stay outside the declared envelope

parameter: Whole-drone sonar blackout (MEDIUM)
source: no source (R2 3e); duty 0.25 %, one or two captures of all six sonars lost
derivation: the data age reaches 0.30 s (0.15 s before the next capture plus the 0.15 s blackout, R1 9.2), above tau_max by design
validity: Exercises FAILSAFE (a sector older than tau_max is unhealthy, sense_ok is false). MEDIUM only

parameter: OCTREE_LEAF_M (sonar octree leaf; cone-edge resolution)
source: simulator setting (holoocean_setup.OCTREE_MIN); the engine sets ShadowEpsilon to OctreeMin for SinglebeamSonar when it is not set (R2 section B)
derivation: angular size of one leaf at range r = atan2(0.06, r)
validity: Enters the detection-cone margin of distance_bound.py

parameter: NEAR_FIELD_WIDEN_M (near-field widening of the structure window)
source: (from simulator measurement, DI-12) at 0.63 m the FRONT sonar returned a gate post 78 deg off its axis, 18 deg outside the nominal 60 deg cone
derivation: widening angle atan(0.25 m / r): 22 deg at 0.6 m, 5 deg at 3 m, 2 deg at 7 m
validity: Changes the prediction of where mapped structure can echo, not the decision thresholds

parameter: MAX_REL_TILT_DEG (tilt of another hull relative to the observer body frame)
source: assumption: BlueROV2-class vehicles are passively stable in roll and pitch; the bound is checked on the logs (distance_bound.py)
derivation: level cylinders inside the hull box for any heading and tilt up to this value (HULL_CYLINDERS)
validity: Role of the tilt assumption is exercised by formal S0 (hull attitude sweep)

parameter: Region-lattice constants (N_DIRS, COVER_RAD, RADII grid, SAMPLING_ERR, RHO_MIN)
source: (from numerical measurement) covering radius of the lattice measured 0.0139 rad (tests/test_distance_bound.py); sampling error = lattice covering radius 0.023 rad + boundary shift between consecutive grid radii 0.02 rad
derivation: certification margin gamma(rho) = (covering radius + region shift) x parallax amplification; RHO_MIN = d_safe
validity: Numerical discretisation of the region tables; certifications hold only with this margin

parameter: structure_tol_m and structure_tol_far_m (echo explained by the gate map)
source: (from the sonar noise model, DI-14) exponential range noise acts per octree leaf: the farthest of about 10^3 leaves lies about 0.05 ln N = 0.4 m beyond the surface, so structure echoes are lengthened on the far side only
derivation: R2 2d: at MEDIUM range_sigma 0.10 the expected maximum over N = 100 / 300 / 1000 leaves is 0.52 / 0.63 / 0.75 m, and P(at least one leaf beyond 0.70 m) = 0.09 / 0.24 / 0.60 per capture (8e-5 to 8e-4 at 0.05)
validity: Open issue O-2: a segment whose last bin passes sw[1] + 0.70 fails in_struct (sonar_processing.py:185) and becomes UNKNOWN or DYNAMIC at the structure's own range. Not verified on logs; cheap check: replay logged MEDIUM profiles with the tolerance scaled to range_sigma

parameter: seabed_tol_m
source: bench observation noted in the code comment: kelp up to about 0.6 m above the DVL bottom (rough, vegetated seabed); no external source
derivation: none
validity: Large against dvl_range_sigma 0.02-0.05 m

parameter: Classifier and tracker constants (merge gap, vehicle extent, confirmation, track drop, closing-rate filter)
source: design constants of the onboard classifier; no external source (DI-11, DI-14, DI-15 give the reasoning for the persistence rule)
derivation: confirmation 2 of 3 trades false alarms (7.6e-2 per capture at MEDIUM) against missed targets (fade, see above)
validity: Persistence costs no safety for hulls in the CR because they are seen for several captures before the bars mask them (formal M4d)

parameter: d_collision (ground-truth centre distance at hull contact, referee only)
source: (from HULL_HALF) side-by-side hull boxes touch at 2 x 0.288 = 0.576 m (computed here); the code comment says BlueROV2 hulls touch around this distance
derivation: 2 x HULL_HALF[1] rounded up
validity: Never read by a controller

parameter: d_safe (P1 requirement G(d >= d_safe))
source: safety requirement chosen by the project; no external source
derivation: equals sonar_geometry.RHO_MIN (region tables start at d_safe)
validity: Ground-truth distance, referee only; the guards compare the conservative onboard distance with d_ca and d_warning

parameter: d_warning
source: (from formal check S1b/S1c) smallest d_warning verified by BMC bisection and k-induction = 1.840 m; configured 2.4 m (margin 0.56 m keeps escapes rare: liveness); mutation d_warning = 1.59 must violate P1 (SAT)
derivation: pairwise radial model with c_max = 1.20 m/s, a_pair = 2 a_brake, d_hat <= d (S0)
validity: Valid under the assumptions listed in check_separation.py (detection inside the 60 deg cone, a_brake, w_rel_max, velocity caps)

parameter: d_warning_exit, d_ca, d_ca_exit, d_nominal
source: hysteresis and trigger levels chosen by the project. config.py states that d_ca is the smallest proven value plus a margin; formal/results/separation.json reports the smallest verified d_warning only (1.840 m)
derivation: d_nominal = smallest inter-slot distance of every formation template; d_warning_exit - d_warning = 0.3 m
validity: Ordering d_nominal > d_warning_exit > d_warning > d_ca_exit > d_ca > d_safe > d_collision holds for these values

parameter: dt (controller period)
source: equal to the 10 Hz capture period of the sonar and the DVL; no external source
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: tau_max (maximum age of the sonar data used by a guard)
source: (from design: 10 Hz capture period + one dropped capture + margin) measured maximum age 0.0 s on the CLEAN reference runs (results/reference/ASSUMPTIONS.md, A2) (R1 9.2, R2 3f)
derivation: with the MEDIUM latency 0.05 s the data age just before the next capture is 0.15 s and one dropped capture reaches exactly 0.25 s (R1); R2 reaches the same boundary after two consecutive drops (1e-4 at 1 %), counting a fresh capture as age 0 (ASSUMPTIONS.md A2): the reports differ by one capture in the age convention
validity: Open issue O-7: MEDIUM has zero margin on tau_max; a MEDIUM blackout (0.15 s) exceeds it by design

parameter: eps_range_far and eps_range_near (echo may lie this much farther or nearer than the true near surface)
source: (from simulator measurement, class d, R2 3a) Phase 1 noise off: error +0.004 to +0.054 m (BlueROV2 head-on), +0.013 broadside, +0.025 box, -0.015 pillar, +0.035 top bar, -0.037 to -0.001 gate opening; CLEAN noise a stable +0.054 m; noise probe max +0.094 m at MultSigma 0.30 or RangeSigma 0.40, +0.144 m at MultSigma 0.60. No external anchor
derivation: the value matches the measured maxima (0.054 plus margin). An earlier comment in config.py decomposed 0.12 as one 5 cm bin + 6 cm leaf + 5 cm threshold bias, which sums to 0.16 m (R2 3a); the comment now states the measured maximum plus margin
validity: HoloOcean 2.3.0 only (leaf 0.06 m, 5 cm bins, threshold 0.30, CLEAN or LOW engine noise). Real deployments add a sound-speed scale term abs(dc/c) x r. MEDIUM jitter exceeds both values (O-1); the comment of eps_range_far now records this (about 0.6 % of captures per side)
code_action: changed: comment corrected and MEDIUM exceedance recorded; values unchanged; open issue O-1

parameter: w_rel_max and w_drift_max (unrejected residual drift)
source: (from simulator calibration, R1 3.1) station-keeping lateral residual drift 0.034 m/s at 0.60 m/s current and 0.158 m/s at 0.80 m/s
derivation: residuals after the low-level loop has compensated the current
validity: Hold only while the requested velocity is control-feasible against the raw current (control/current_envelope.py); persistent saturation violates them and the onboard monitor declares ENVELOPE_VIOLATION (DI-24, DI-27)

parameter: g_min and v_open (certified escape opening, warning-filter opening)
source: design requirements; checked by formal S2a (worst certified guarantee 0.511) and S2b (worst certified opening 0.202 m/s)
derivation: sampling error of the direction tables (0.045) already subtracted
validity: Exhaustive over the 26 sector patterns

parameter: struct_keepout
source: never close on mapped structure nearer than this; no external source
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: Operating depth band (world z, up positive)
source: scenario design; no external source
derivation: none
validity: Also used by the acoustic depth check (AcousticConfig.depth_tol_m)

parameter: c_max (worst-case pair closing speed) and v_close_staleness
source: (from Envelope) c_max = v_escape + v_max_nominal + w_rel_max = 0.55 + 0.50 + 0.15; v_close_staleness is set equal to it
derivation: one drone escaping, one cruising, plus differential drift
validity: Measured back on the reference runs: A3 maximum closing speed 0.794 m/s (results/reference/ASSUMPTIONS.md)

parameter: Critical region (CR) half extents (length, width, height)
source: protocol geometry chosen by the project; the code states no derivation. The half-width equals half of the 2.0 m opening quoted in structure_aiding.py
derivation: none
validity: Gate frame: s along the axis towards the exit, l left, z up

parameter: queue_spacing
source: chosen to satisfy a derived inequality (code comment): larger than d_warning_exit + estimate margin, so queued neighbours never trigger the warning
derivation: 3.5 m > 2.7 m + margin; equals d_nominal
validity: Measured back: closest pair of queued drones 3.447-3.510 m on the reference runs (ASSUMPTIONS.md A4; formal M4c needs spacing - 2 x 0.10 m)

parameter: queue_cone_deg
source: (from sonar geometry) CR bearing from every queue sonar must stay inside the sonar half-angle
derivation: 49 + heading_tol 6 + hull fuzz 5 = 60 deg = SonarModel.half_angle_deg
validity: Formal M4a (queue line); mutation M4m (queue line at s = -4 m) must violate it

parameter: queue_tol and heading_tol_deg
source: tolerances chosen by the project; no external source
derivation: none
validity: Enter the sector-rule tolerance box of the formal precedence checks (M2)

parameter: hold_err_m (position-holding error of a queued drone)
source: (from simulator measurement) the code comment cites results/reference/ASSUMPTIONS.md (A4: queued neighbours at least spacing - 2 x 0.10 m apart)
derivation: none
validity: Simulator figure (CLEAN, DVL velocity loop)

parameter: Approach zone and bracket (approach_len, corridor_half_width, queue_bracket_m)
source: geometry chosen by the project (DI-23 for the outer queue points of n >= 5); no external source
derivation: none
validity: queue_bracket_m equals FormationRule.neighbour_range_m

parameter: t_clear and t_occ_max
source: protocol timers chosen by the project. t_occ_max is a fallback: the CR belief returns FREE after it without corridor echoes (logged as a timeout)
derivation: safe only if a healthy occupant crosses the CR within t_occ_max (formal M3, crossing speed >= V_LO = 0.12 m/s; measured minimum 0.478-0.487 m/s, ASSUMPTIONS.md A5)
validity: A drone stopped inside the CR by a fault and masked by the bars is outside the guarantee (formal M3f counterexample). Variant B2 does not release the CR by this fallback while a fresh accepted acoustic fix places a drone possibly inside it (acoustic_gate.heard_inside)

parameter: Pass-path geometry and speeds
source: pass-path design (DI-17, DI-28); no external source
derivation: v_approach = v_pass = Envelope.v_max_nominal
validity: Pass-path clearance and stacked-queue geometry are checked by formal M4s

parameter: stack_column_spacing and stack_spacing
source: chosen so that a diagonal neighbour is always seen in LEFT/RIGHT and a neighbour of the same column only in UP/DOWN (code comment)
derivation: formal M2v / M2vm: columns 3.5 m apart make a diagonal pair ambiguous, so the columns are farther apart than the stack spacing
validity: Every pair stays inside the queue bracket

parameter: queue_lateral_max (validated gate domain)
source: (from formal M4g) queue points from which a sonar exit witness of every passing drone exists: the abreast queue up to 3 drones, the 2 x 2 and 3-drone stacks; beyond it (abreast 4-6, a 3-column stack) the outer drones see no exit and mission.check_gate_domain refuses the passage
derivation: measured detection range used by M4g: R_DETECT_M = 10 m (at least 29 % of captures up to 10 m, 19 % at 10-11 m, 7 % at 11-12 m; results/calibration/gate/exit_detection.json)
validity: Recent change; the audit reports do not cover the gate parameters. For variant B2, formal B2-M4g reports that with the multipath-covering envelope no acoustic exit evidence exists inside this domain: the sonar latch applies (see ACOUSTIC_CHANNEL_MODEL.md section 9)
code_action: recent change: queue_lateral_max introduced (formal M4g, mission.check_gate_domain)

parameter: MAX_CORR_M (largest horizontal correction of the structure aiding)
source: the drift a run can accumulate (code comment); no external source
derivation: a 2 deg bias drifts 3.49 % of the distance; the docstring quotes about 0.5 m after the approach to the gate
validity: A drone whose drift brought it in front of a bar cannot be relocalised by a range-only fit without an assumption on echo identity: it holds (documented C5 limitation)

parameter: acquisition_distance (farthest distance before the gate plane at which a fit can be accepted)
source: (from sonar geometry) a side cone sees a bar point at offset c from the gate axis only when x <= tan(half_angle) abs(c - e); over true offsets abs(e) <= MAX_CORR_M
derivation: tan(60 deg) x (outer half-extent 1.25 m + MAX_CORR_M 1.2 m) = 4.24 m, with outer = 1.0 m half-opening + 0.25 m bar; capped by SonarModel.range_max
validity: Gate with a 2.0 m opening and 0.25 m bars; the code evaluates it from the gate map. Recent change (C5: derived from sonar visibility); the audit reports do not cover it
code_action: recent change: acquisition region derived from sonar visibility (ee63bb8)

parameter: Fit acceptance constants of the structure aiding
source: design constants; validated against the CLEAN runs: the nominal cone predicts the first echo of the horizontal sonars within 0.023-0.026 m (SD) and a bar that is not seen in 0-2 % of the samples (structure_aiding.py)
derivation: HULL_LAT_M = 0.288 + 0.229 sin 5 deg = 0.308 m (computed from HULL_HALF)
validity: Replay of archived MEDIUM runs with range-only fits applied beside the opening was wrong by 0.4-1.2 m, so a fit beside the opening is never applied

parameter: Formation error thresholds (e_lost, e_ok, t_ok_hold; same values in RefereeConfig)
source: thresholds chosen by the project; no external source
derivation: formal F3: the ball abs(e) <= e* is invariant with e* = 0.44 m along and 0.36 m lateral, below e_ok
validity: A4 needs the onboard form_err below e_ok

parameter: Slot-tracking and sonar-correction gains
source: controller gains; no external source
derivation: ranking decreases certified in the saturated and linear bands (formal F1, F2); mutations k_slot = 0 and no catch-up margin are caught
validity: Abstraction of the deployed formation law under explicit fairness and environment assumptions (check_formation.py)

parameter: Speed caps while following and recovering
source: design caps; v_recovery_max equals Envelope.v_max_nominal
derivation: catch-up margin v_recovery_max - v_nominal = 0.2 m/s
validity: Deliverable against head currents only up to about 0.21 m/s at 0.5 m/s (DI-27)

parameter: Association, range and re-inclusion constants
source: design constants; no external source
derivation: none
validity: neighbour_range_m equals GateRule.queue_bracket_m and enters t_rejoin

parameter: v_wait and a_wait (reduced progress while a neighbour is missing)
source: compromise argued in DI-31 and the config.py comment: catch-up of a rejoining drone grows from 0.20 to 0.30 m/s; the along-track offset between drones noticing an absence at different times grows at v_nominal - v_wait = 0.10 m/s, so a detection spread of 7 s stays below e_ok after the ramp (0.10 x (7 - T_ramp / 2) = 0.45 m)
derivation: a_wait ramps 0.30 to 0.20 m/s in 5 s, far below the braking capability a_brake
validity: Never zero: the fleet keeps surveying and keeps steerage

parameter: t_rejoin (derived) with t_rejoin_margin and t_rejoin_max
source: (from the catch-up speed) t_rejoin = min(60, neighbour_range_m / (v_recovery_max - v_wait) + margin) = min(60, 7.5 / 0.30 + 5.0) = 30 s
derivation: the gap is a configured bound, not an onboard estimate; the margin covers ramp-in (about 0.8 s), confirmation (up to 1 s) and the final approach (about 1.5 s), rounded up
validity: Formal F6 (BMC over ceil(t_rejoin / dt) + 1 steps) and F6r (ranking): a neighbour that never reappears is declared vacant and the drone leaves FORMATION_WAIT_REJOIN

parameter: follow_on_m, follow_off_m, a_follow (spacing to the drone ahead)
source: code comment: follow_on lies above the calm-flight residual (one 5 cm range bin); a_follow = 2.5 a_wait keeps the compression below about 0.14 m when the drone ahead slows at a_wait
derivation: none
validity: Prevents a rear drone at the survey speed from closing on a slowed one (the same-lane warning band at 3.5 m starts about 0.23 m closer)

parameter: H2: synchronised clocks (one-way travel-time ranging; CSAC or OCXO disciplined to GNSS PPS before the dive)
source: (a) SA.45s CSAC datasheet: 1 PPS discipline to within 1 ns and 1.0E-12, retrace +-5e-10, aging below 9e-10 per month; (b) field demonstrations of synchronous-clock OWTT: Rypkema 2022 with a CSAC, Eustice 2011 and Webster 2012 with a low-power TCXO (R3 H2, Q1)
derivation: see sound_speed_err and clock_offset_m below
validity: Never power-cycled during the dive; sender PPS-to-emission jitter well below 30 us

parameter: H3: calibrated 3-D inverted-USBL receiving array on every drone
source: R3 H3: feasible as research hardware on small AUVs (Rypkema 2022 five-hydrophone pyramid, Jakuba 2021 four-element 38 mm array, Raspi2USBL six elements), not a COTS feature
derivation: none
validity: Must be 3-D and calibrated: published planar arrays are worst for neighbours near the horizontal plane. Feasibility evidence is class (b); the CLEAN and LOW magnitudes at 2-20 m between moving BlueROV2-class vehicles are not demonstrated in the field

parameter: sigma_range_m (detection jitter, white, per reception)
source: (a) SeaTrac range resolution +-0.1 m (two-way, depends on the velocity of sound provided), MicronNav 200 +-0.2 m; (b) WHOI Micro-Modem OWTT TOA 125 us = 18.75 cm, ranges set at 18.75 cm std; ahoi two-way static: 50 % of values within 6 cm of the median; Rypkema 2022 one-way static: 68 % of range errors below 0.7 m (about 30 and 57 m, 7-11 kHz) (R3 P1)
derivation: one detection with timing jitter sigma_t gives c sigma_t one-way but c sigma_t / sqrt(2) for a round trip, so a two-way +-0.1 m is about +-0.14 m one-way; matched-filter resolution c / (2B): 0.375 m (B = 2 kHz), 0.15 m (5 kHz), 0.094 m (8 kHz)
validity: CLEAN and LOW assume a wideband (5-8 kHz or more), well-calibrated detector at 2-20 m; MEDIUM sits at the datasheet end and no level reaches the published one-way field figure (open issue O-11). The jitter must also contain the sender trigger jitter, which a two-way figure never shows

parameter: sound_speed_err (relative std of c_assumed; one range scale factor per run)
source: (from physics, R3 P2) OWTT range = c_assumed x travel time, so the relative range error equals the relative error of c_assumed; Mackenzie partial derivatives dc/dT = 4.08 / 3.60 / 3.16 / 2.75 m/s per deg C at 5 / 10 / 15 / 20 deg C, dc/dS 1.14-1.29 m/s per psu; refraction is negligible at 2-50 m in one layer
derivation: 0.3 % = 4.5 m/s, about 1.4 deg C at 15 deg C or 3.8 psu; 1 % = 15 m/s, about 4.7 deg C or 12.5 psu
validity: Valid only if c_assumed is computed onboard from temperature, depth and a known salinity. CONTRADICTED (R3 P2) for an uncompensated 1500 m/s: field sound speeds of 1426-1481 m/s would be off by 1.3 % to 5.2 %. Code action: H2 in the acoustic_channel.py docstring now states the onboard estimate
code_action: changed: the onboard sound-speed estimate is an explicit assumption (docstring H2)

parameter: clock_offset_m (std of a drone clock offset expressed as a range; constant per run)
source: (a) SA.45s CSAC; (b) Rypkema 2022: CSACs drift less than 100 us per 24 h in holdover; Jakuba 2021: CSAC about 1 ppb against about 20 ppb for a TCXO; Eustice 2011: TCXO 20 ns/s typical, below 300 us per 24 h on the bench, below 4 us in a 1.5 h dive (R3 P3)
derivation: a constant fractional frequency offset y gives a range error c y t; per ppb over 1 h: 5.4 mm (c = 1500 m/s). Table in ACOUSTIC_CHANNEL_MODEL.md section 4
validity: CLEAN bounds a CSAC over 1 h; LOW and MEDIUM correspond to an OCXO or a measured TCXO over 1 h, or to uncalibrated constant hardware delays. A TCXO at 20 ns/s reaches 0.11 m per drone (0.22 m between two drones) after 1 h, i.e. the 0.21 m envelope bound. For longer missions model offset0 + drift t

parameter: sigma_az_deg and sigma_el_deg (direction of arrival, white, receiver body frame)
source: (a) SeaTrac X150 angular resolution typ. 2 % of range (about +-1 deg), MicronNav 200 1 deg RMS (limited by the heading sensor), older MicronNav +-3 deg, Micro-Ranger 2 array below 3.5 % of slant range; (b) one-way inverted USBL: Rypkema 2022 68 % of azimuth errors below 7.0 deg (static, about 30 and 57 m), Rypkema 2019 -0.11 +- 3.16 deg, Jakuba 2021 better than +-5 deg at low tilt (R3 P4)
derivation: none (values copied)
validity: CLEAN and LOW match two-way micro-USBL datasheets that include a heading sensor; MEDIUM is below every published one-way field value. The dominant error of field systems, the array bias, is now a separate term (doa_bias_deg); the remaining gap is open issue O-11

parameter: doa_bias_deg (array calibration residual: smooth, direction-dependent, fixed per receiver)
source: phenomenon supported (b): Jakuba 2021 find the arrival-angle error dominated by bias; Rypkema 2022 angle bias depends on azimuth and frequency, largest ahead and astern; R3 P4 recommended a per-run direction-dependent bias of a few degrees. The amplitudes are stress values
derivation: per axis b(az) = A (sin(az + p1) + sin(2 az + p2)) / 2 with phases p uniform per receiver and axis, so abs(b) <= A. For MEDIUM (A = 3.0 deg, white 2.5 deg) the 68 % quantile of the azimuth error is at most 4.2 deg (normal CDF, computed here), below the 7.0 deg of the static river test
validity: New since R3 (before the final campaign); only makes the channel harsher. Onboard counterpart: AcousticConfig.doa_bias_deg

parameter: dropout and dropout_far (per-reception loss at short range and at max_range_m)
source: (b) ahoi marina test: 97.1 % received at 12 m (91.5-99.5 % at the three good positions at 12, 46 and 99 m), 57.5 % at 24 m, 8.0 % at 152 m; moving uAUV request reception 79-94 %, 70-80 % near a pillar; static two-way ranging 1.8 % lost (R3 P5)
derivation: p = dropout + (dropout_far - dropout) min(1, d / 50 m); at 2-20 m: 0.023-0.052 (CLEAN), 0.087-0.148 (LOW), 0.212-0.320 (MEDIUM)
validity: Magnitudes lie inside the measured envelope of a low-cost modem in a harbour at 10-100 m. The model draws independent losses with a linear range ramp, whereas measured loss is position-dependent, not monotonic in range and correlated in time; ahoi figures are 292-476 ms packets, not short identity pings

parameter: Burst outages (MEDIUM): outage_every_s and outage_len_s
source: phenomenon supported qualitatively (R3 P6): an acoustic payload can mask or falsely trigger an LBL response (Olson); bursty channel behaviour (ahoi); machinery noise (Li 2025) and impulsive noise (Chitre 2008). No source quantifies outage rates or durations for 20-30 kHz pings near thrusters
derivation: first start uniform in [4, 40] s, then exponential gaps (mean 40 s) + 4 s: about 9 % of the time
validity: A sweep over outage length (1-10 s) would show the sensitivity

parameter: nlos_rx (blocked direct path: probability that a reflected arrival is detected)
source: no source gives this conditional probability; Olson's over 25 % is an unconditional outlier fraction of one long-range LBL example (R3 P7)
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: reflect_extra_m (extra path of a reflected arrival; also the excess of a clear-path multipath episode)
source: (from geometry, R3 P7b) single surface or bottom bounce between two drones at the same distance h from the boundary, separation d: extra path = sqrt(d^2 + 4 h^2) - d
validity: Valid for operation 1-3 m from a reflecting boundary and separations of at least 3 m; deeper operation or shorter separations give up to 7-8 m

parameter: reflect_dir_deg (direction error of a reflected arrival)
unit: deg (elevation std; azimuth std 0.2 x 25 = 5 deg)
source: R3 P7c: geometry gives elevation-dominated, signed errors of 5-70 deg for a surface or bottom bounce (a vertical wall errs in azimuth); the magnitude is a stress value
derivation: arrival elevation = atan(2 h / d): 34 / 22 / 11 / 6 deg at d = 3 / 5 / 10 / 20 m for h = 1 m
validity: Changed since R3: R3 read N(0, 25 deg) on both axes; the code now draws 5 deg in azimuth and 25 deg in elevation (boundary bounces err mainly in elevation)

parameter: shadow_loss (direct path shadowed by a hull or a gate bar: ping lost)
source: Fresnel premise DERIVED (below), loss in dB not calibrated by any source (R3 P8). ahoi mobile data show about 18 dB of receive-gain headroom at 50 m, so a few dB of diffraction loss would rarely cause a loss at 2-20 m: 0.3-0.7 is likely pessimistic
derivation: first Fresnel radius at mid-path r1 = 0.5 sqrt(lambda d), 20-30 kHz at 1500 m/s: 0.19-0.24 m at 3 m, 0.35-0.43 m at 10 m (the earlier 0.3-0.5 m overstated 3 m)
validity: The BlueROV2 box (0.458 x 0.576 x 0.254 m) is comparable to r1 at 3-5 m and smaller beyond: partial obstruction, so diffraction filling the shadow is plausible. An air-filled electronics tube reflects strongly, so the shadow need not be weak (physical reasoning only)
code_action: changed: Fresnel numbers corrected in the docstring

parameter: shadow_extra_m and shadow_dir_deg (diffracted arrival)
source: (from geometry, R3 P8b) extra path of the diffracted arrival around an edge offset a at mid-path: 2 (sqrt(d^2 / 4 + a^2) - d / 2)
derivation: 0.10 m at d = 1 m and 0.035 m at d = 3 m for a = 0.23 m, so 0.10 m is conservative for d of 1 m or more. shadow_dir_deg is a STRESS ASSUMPTION (R3 P8c)
validity: Covered onboard by RANGE_SLACK_M = 0.15 m

parameter: latency_s (processing delay after the arrival)
source: (a) Water Linked M64 about 500 ms typical latency (a communication modem, includes packet duration); (b) Huang 2026: acoustic positioning delays of several hundred ms to a few s (citing others), measured piUSBL system delay about 8 ms; Rypkema 2022: one particle-filter iteration about 500 ms on a Raspberry Pi 3 (R3 P9)
derivation: physical lower bound: detection cannot end before the whole coded ping (20-40 ms) has arrived; no SeaTrac, MicronNav, Micro-Ranger 2 or UGPS latency figure was found
validity: Inside the 8 ms - 0.5 s bracket; the onboard staleness bound latency_max_s = 0.40 s is consistent

parameter: los_outlier, CLEAN level: a clear direct path gives no range outlier
source: R3 P7: field reports of multipath false maxima and of line-of-sight and boundary-path cancellation without any blocking object contradict the premise (Webster 2012: ranges often not Gaussian, false ranges from multipath; Olson 2006: multipath errors can affect several successive measurements; Rypkema 2022: false maxima in an unobstructed river; Renner 2020: probable cancellation at 24 m with a clear path)
derivation: none
validity: Code action: LOW and MEDIUM now model multipath episodes (next row); CLEAN keeps 0 as the idealised baseline level, by definition
code_action: changed: episodes added at LOW and MEDIUM; CLEAN idealised

parameter: los_outlier (LOW, MEDIUM) and los_outlier_pings: clear-path multipath episodes
source: phenomenon supported (b) by the field reports listed in the previous row; no source gives the probability of an episode or its length (channel docstring: stress values)
derivation: with probability los_outlier per reception an episode starts on the link and lasts los_outlier_pings receptions on average; the time of arrival is that of a boundary bounce, longer by a fixed excess drawn once per episode from reflect_extra_m, while the array still resolves the direct path: slowly varying ranges that mimic valid data (Olson)
validity: Added after R3, before the final campaign; only makes the channel harsher. Onboard counterpart: AcousticConfig.los_excess_max_m

parameter: TDMA slot length and collision handling (guard_s removed)
source: (from design and geometry, R3 P10 and P11) collision freedom of the TDMA schedule: the slot exceeds the worst propagation spread at 50 m (33 ms) plus a 20-40 ms ping. TDMA requires good time synchronisation (Chitre 2008); collisions grow with the number of transmitters (Binder 2016)
derivation: slot = period_ticks // n ticks at 30 Hz, giving 500 / 333 / 233 / 200 / 167 ms for n = 2..6. R3: guard_s (10 ms) was defined but never read and is shorter than any real ping
validity: Code action: the unused guard_s field was removed from AcousticChannel. The applied rule (beacon.py): pings whose engine results can share one receiver buffer (2-tick window, 67 ms) are all lost; it never triggers with slots of 167 ms or more. Identities are static codes: receivers are assumed able to separate distinct pinger codes

parameter: period_s (ping period)
source: (b) Rypkema 2022: one-way beacon at 1 Hz triggered by the GPS PPS; Jakuba 2021: sweeps at 4 Hz; products 2-4 Hz (UGPS G2), up to 3 Hz (Micro-Ranger 2) (R3 P11)
derivation: none
validity: Webster 2012 notes modem-packet ranges are not typically made every second: a statement about data packets, not identity pings

parameter: max_range_m (engine range limit)
source: (a) all verified products exceed it: SeaTrac 1 km, MicronNav 200 500 m horizontal, Micro-Ranger 2 below 995 m, M64 200 m; ahoi reliable at 150 m (R3 P12)
derivation: none
validity: Conservative. The scenarios use 2-20 m; the 50 m point only anchors the dropout ramp

parameter: sound_speed (propagation constant for the delivery delay)
source: (from nominal value, R3 P13) Li 2025 give about 1500 m/s; opened sources span 1426-1540 m/s
derivation: delay = distance / sound_speed
validity: Harmless as a propagation constant: a 5 % error shifts delivery by less than 2 ms over 50 m. It is not the onboard c_assumed (see sound_speed_err)

parameter: check_visible and BLACKOUT level
source: simulator settings. CheckVisible is a single engine ray that any hull or prop blocks; the channel model turns hull and bar blockage into shadowing (H4). BLACKOUT tests the fall-back to B0
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: k_sigma
source: (from the Gaussian) P(abs(z) > 3) = 0.27 % per axis, 0.81 % for at least one of three independent axes (R3 P14)
derivation: the envelope uses the MEDIUM sigmas, so CLEAN and LOW receptions lie well inside
validity: Heavy tails are documented (Webster Fig. 14, Olson 2006, Rypkema 2022), so the real exceedance is higher; the residual risk is measured (calibration/analyze_b2_channel.py), not claimed

parameter: sigma_range_m, sigma_az_deg, sigma_el_deg (declared white sigmas)
source: (from the MEDIUM channel) equal to the MEDIUM white sigmas
derivation: none
validity: Declared before any B2 result; the perception never knows the channel level of a run

parameter: sound_speed_err (declared scale error)
source: (from the MEDIUM channel) 3 x 1 %
derivation: range half-width term 0.03 r
validity: Violated by an uncompensated 1500 m/s (marina 3.6 % and 5.2 %); requires the onboard c estimate of H2

parameter: clock_offset_m (declared bias between two clocks)
source: (from the MEDIUM channel) 3 x sqrt(2) x 0.05 m = 0.212 m: the offset difference of two drones
derivation: none
validity: A TCXO at 20 ns/s typical spec reaches it in 1 h (R3 P3)

parameter: doa_bias_deg (declared array calibration bias)
source: (from the MEDIUM channel) amplitude of the MEDIUM array bias
derivation: azimuth and elevation half-widths each include it
validity: Added after R3, before the final campaign

parameter: los_excess_max_m (one-sided range extension for clear-path multipath)
source: (from the channel) upper bound of reflect_extra_m; the measured range can be this much too long, so the error region reaches this much nearer
derivation: acoustic.region_samples: range samples from max(r - br - 3.0, 0) to r + br
validity: Added after R3. Consequence (formal B2-M4g): regions this large leave no acoustic exit evidence in the validated gate geometry; the sonar latch applies there

parameter: heading_err_deg
source: code comment: own compass bias plus noise (MEDIUM bias 2.0 deg); no external source
derivation: 2.0 deg MEDIUM bias + 1.0 deg allowance for noise
validity: Open issue O-8 (derived here from R1 6.2 and nav.py): the allowance is below one std of the MEDIUM per-sample heading noise (57.3 x 0.02 = 1.15 deg); at k_sigma = 3 the bound would be 2.0 + 3 x 1.15 = 5.4 deg

parameter: tilt_err_deg
source: code comment: own unestimated roll and pitch of a BlueROV2 holding depth; no external source (the fix rotation uses the heading only)
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: v_bound (speed bound of a neighbour used by the kinematic gate)
source: (from Envelope and GateRule) max(v_escape, v_max_nominal, v_pass) + w_drift_max = 0.55 + 0.15
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: Error-box half-widths of a fix at range r (summary of the fields above)
source: (from AcousticConfig) range 3 x 0.15 + 0.03 r + 0.21; azimuth 3 x 2.5 + 3.0 + 3.0; elevation 3 x 2.5 + 3.0 + 3.0
derivation: sampled 7 x 7 x 7 with a slack of half the diagonal of a grid cell
validity: Formal B2-A1: 4000 random measurements at 0.5-30 m, worst -0.017 m (must be 0 or below)

parameter: latency_max_s (a delivery later than this after its arrival is not used)
source: R3 P9: consistent with the published 8 ms - 0.5 s bracket and with the MEDIUM channel latency 0.25 s
derivation: none
validity: none stated

parameter: nav_err_gate_m (own position error in the gate frame)
source: code comment: bounded by the map aiding; R1 section 8 finds it equal to a 28.6 m approach at a 2 deg bias (27.5 m with a 1 % DVL scale factor), while MEDIUM runs reported in R1 reach 0.7-1.1 m
derivation: D sin b = 1.0 m for D = 28.6 m at b = 2 deg
validity: Open issue O-6. R1: cap the approach distance used in the gate argument or raise it to about 1.2 m if the DVL scale factor is added

parameter: track_gate_m and RANGE_SLACK_M (kinematic-gate slacks)
source: code comments: RANGE_SLACK_M covers the diffracted excess of a shadowed path (shadow_extra_m = 0.10 m) and quantisation
derivation: RANGE_SLACK_M >= shadow_extra_m
validity: The gate budgets the white part of the errors only (biases are common to two fixes and cancel)

parameter: exit_confirm (consecutive accepted fixes for an acoustic exit)
source: (from simulation) calibration/analyze_b2_channel.py, 20 000 trials per level: wrong 'outside the CR' decisions with exit_confirm = 2: 9 / 58 / 129 in about 65 000 receptions (CLEAN / LOW / MEDIUM); with 3: 0 / 3 / 3; wrong 'beyond the exit face': 0 in about 200 000
derivation: a wrong decision needs consecutive accepted reflections
validity: Open issue O-12: measured before the envelope was widened (doa_bias_deg, los_excess_max_m) and not re-run for this document (channel_risk.json is dated 2026-10-29 02:00, the code 22:46)

parameter: tie_window_s, fresh_s, depth_tol_m, REINIT_S, _KEEP_S
source: design constants; fresh_s is described as one lost ping plus the latency (period 1.0 s + 1.0 s + MEDIUM latency 0.25 s = 2.25 s, computed here, against 2.5 s in the code); depth_tol_m: a fix this far outside the operating depth band is a reflection
derivation: none
validity: The depth check uses Envelope.z_min and z_max
